# News Reader

> News is a calm, local-first RSS/Atom feed reader for phone and desktop (installable web app, works offline). Every entry gets one decision: read now, later or not interested. Devices sync end-to-end encrypted (AES-256-GCM) without an account or database. It ships with the Collector, a REST endpoint that turns any website – with or without an RSS feed – into normalized JSON entries. Open source (MIT), self-hostable and white-label; server side is plain PHP 8.5+, no build step.

Project by kreativ-anders (https://kreativ-anders.de). Home: https://news-reader.app/.

Key facts:

- Components: `app/` (the News PWA, plain ES modules, IndexedDB), `api/index.php` (front controller), `/api/sync` (encrypted sync), `/api/collect` (Collector).
- Not a hosted SaaS with accounts: there is no sign-up, no cookies, no ads, no user profiles; fonts are self-hosted. news-reader.app counts visits with cookie-free Pirsch Analytics (self-hosters remove or replace the snippet, see README → White-label).
- Sync: the first device creates a random 32-byte vault key; other devices join by pasting the pairing link (`app/#pair=<key>`) into Settings → Sync, or by opening it. HKDF-SHA256 derives a bearer token and an AES-256-GCM key from it. The server stores one opaque encrypted blob per vault (file named after the hash of the token) and never sees the key. Losing all devices means the vault cannot be decrypted; OPML export backs up the feed list (not reading states).
- Collector resolution order: platform rule (known page URLs of Medium, YouTube, Reddit, GitHub, Mastodon etc. mapped to their native feed without fetching the page) → direct feed (RSS 2.0, RSS 1.0/RDF, Atom) → feed declared in HTML (`discovered`) → common feed paths (`guessed`) → sitemap (only if it has at least 3 entries and at least half of them carry a date) → HTML extraction as last resort (JSON-LD, `<article>`, links below the requested path).
- Collector API: `GET /api/collect?url=<url>[&refresh=1][&limit=1..100]` → `{source, entries[{id,url,title,publishedAt,updatedAt,summary,image,author}], meta}`; errors as `{error:{code,message}}` with 400 (invalid URL) or 422 (source failed / no feed), 429 rate limited, 503 busy. If the source answers 401/403, the error carries `clientTry[]` – addresses the app fetches from the user's own browser (e.g. the WordPress REST API); it posts the body to `POST /api/collect?url=…&from=…` (max. 1 MB), which parses it for that caller only and caches nothing. 24 h shared cache, stale copies up to 7 days, SSRF protection (private hosts blocked, every redirect re-validated), per-IP rate limits (only fetches that reach the source count; busy answers are free).
- Migration: OPML import and export – works with virtually every other feed reader.
- Digital sovereignty: run it on your own infrastructure (company, public sector, intranet); no accounts, no database, end-to-end encrypted sync, MIT license without per-seat fees; internal sources on private hosts can be enabled explicitly.
- Languages: English (default), German, French, Italian, Spanish.
- Hosting requirements: PHP 8.5+ with dom, libxml, mbstring (curl recommended), HTTPS, writable `var/`. No database server, no background workers. nginx config included.
